situation: A colleague hasn't replied to your email from Monday, and you need the answer.
say: Gentle reminder!! Please revert ASAP.
better: Just checking in on my email from Monday. Could you reply by Friday so I can close the report?
also: Any update on this? I need it by Friday to finish the report.
weak: Kindly revert at the earliest, waiting for your response since long.
Hello?? Any update??
why: A date and a reason get replies. 'Revert' means go back, not reply.

situation: You are writing the first line of an email to a client.
say: Respected Sir/Madam, I am writing this mail to inform you that...
better: Hi Ms Rao, a quick update on the delivery date for your order.
also: Dear Ms Rao, I'm writing about the delivery date for your order.
weak: Respected Sir, PFA the details as discussed for your kind perusal.
Dear Sir, this is to bring to your kind notice that...
why: Get to the point in the first line; drop old-fashioned formulas.

situation: You lost track of a point during a meeting.
say: Sorry, I didn't get you. Come again?
better: Sorry, I lost you at the pricing part. Could you go over that again?
also: Could you give me an example? I want to be sure I've understood.
weak: Okay okay, understood. (You haven't.)
What are you saying? It's not clear at all.
why: Name exactly which part lost you; pretending wastes everyone's time later.

situation: You need Friday off for a cousin's wedding.
say: Sir, I want leave tomorrow, my cousin's marriage is there.
better: I'd like to take Friday off for a family wedding. Neha has agreed to cover my client call.
also: Can I take Friday off for a wedding? My work is covered.
weak: Sir, kindly grant me leave, it's very urgent, please sir.
I'm taking tomorrow off, FYI.
why: Ask early, give the date, and show your work is covered.

situation: A job offer comes in lower than you expected.
say: Sir, please do something about the package, it's too less.
better: Thank you for the offer. Based on my experience and the market, I was expecting ₹18 lakh. Is there room to move?
also: I'm excited about the role. Could we get closer to ₹18 lakh?
weak: Whatever you feel is right, sir, I'm okay with anything.
This is too less. My friend is getting double somewhere else.
why: Name a number and a reason. 'Too less' is vague, and wrong: say 'too low'.

situation: In your appraisal, you want to ask for a raise.
say: I have worked very hard this year, so I deserve a good hike.
better: This year I cut our delivery time by 20% and took over two accounts. I'd like a raise that reflects that.
also: Here are three results from this year. Can we talk about my pay?
weak: Everyone else got a good hike, so why not me?
Sir, I leave it to you, whatever you think is best.
why: Results speak louder than 'hard work'. Bring numbers.

situation: Your manager criticises your work during the appraisal.
say: But sir, that was not my fault, the other team delayed.
better: That's fair. Can you give me an example, so I know what to do differently next quarter?
also: Thanks for being direct. What would good look like here?
weak: Okay sir, sorry sir, it won't happen again sir.
Everyone does the same thing, why only me?
why: Ask for specifics before defending yourself. It shows you can take feedback.

situation: You disagree with your manager's plan in a team meeting.
say: With due respect sir, you are wrong.
better: I see it differently. Last month's numbers point the other way. Can I show you?
also: I have a concern about this plan. Can I explain?
weak: Sir, whatever you say is correct, but... no, nothing.
That idea won't work at all.
why: Disagree with the idea using facts, not with the person.

situation: Your manager hands you new work when your week is already full.
say: Sir, I have too much on my plate, I can't do.
better: I can take this on, but then the vendor report will slip to next week. Which matters more?
also: My week is full. Could this wait till Monday, or should I drop something?
weak: Okay sir, I'll manage somehow.
Why always me? Give it to someone else.
why: Show the trade-off and let your manager choose the priority.

situation: You join a video call ten minutes late.
say: Sorry sorry, I was stuck in another call, network issue also.
better: Sorry I'm late. Please carry on; I'll catch up from the notes.
also: Apologies for the delay. Don't let me hold you up.
weak: Sorry, there was so much traffic, then my laptop also hung, then...
Hi all, I'm here now, can you start from the beginning?
why: Apologise once, briefly, and don't make the meeting about you.

situation: You're stuck on an Excel formula and need a colleague's help.
say: Can you do one thing? Just do this for me quickly.
better: Do you have 15 minutes today to help me with this Excel formula? I'm stuck.
also: Could you look at this when you're free? I'm stuck on one formula.
weak: Just do the needful and send it to me.
You know Excel na, just finish this for me.
why: Say exactly what you need and how long it takes. Respect their time.

situation: A client spots that you sent them the wrong invoice.
say: Sorry for the inconvenience caused, it was a technical glitch.
better: You're right, we sent the wrong invoice. The correct one is attached, and we've added a check so it won't happen again.
also: That was our mistake. Here's the corrected invoice.
weak: Inconvenience regretted. Kindly ignore the previous mail.
It was not from our side, the system did it.
why: Own the mistake, fix it, and say how you'll stop it happening again.

situation: A meeting is running long and nothing is being decided.
say: Okay, so we will connect offline and do the needful.
better: Let's stop here. Arjun will send the action points by 5, and we'll meet again on Thursday.
also: We're out of time. Quick recap: Arjun owns pricing, Meena owns the timeline.
weak: Okay guys, let's take it offline, will discuss.
Any other points? Anyone? No? Okay... anything else?
why: End with who does what by when, not a vague 'offline'.

situation: You introduce yourself on your first day in a new team.
say: Myself Rohit, from Kanpur, I have done my B.Tech from...
better: Hi, I'm Rohit. I've joined as a data analyst, and I'll mostly work on the sales dashboards.
also: Hi everyone, I'm Rohit, the new analyst. Happy to help with any data questions.
weak: Myself Rohit, and I am very much excited to join this esteemed organisation.
Hi, Rohit here. That's it.
why: Say 'I'm Rohit', not 'myself Rohit', and tell people what you'll do here.

situation: Your boss messages at 10 pm about work that isn't urgent.
say: Sure sir, will do it right now.
better: Got it. I'll look at this first thing tomorrow morning.
also: Noted. You'll have it by 11 tomorrow.
weak: Sir, it's 10 pm, office hours are over.
Okay sir, I'll stay up and finish it, no problem sir.
why: Acknowledge it and give a clear time, without being rude or always available.

situation: You're telling your manager that you are resigning.
say: Sir, I have got a better offer, so I am putting my papers.
better: I wanted you to hear it from me first: I've accepted another role. My last day will be 30 June.
also: I've decided to move on. I'll make sure the handover is smooth.
weak: Sorry to say, but this place has no growth, so I'm resigning.
I'm leaving. HR will tell you the details.
why: Be clear and gracious. Don't criticise the place you're leaving.

situation: Your travel claim from last month still hasn't been paid.
say: Why my reimbursement is still not done? I am waiting since one month.
better: My travel claim from 3 May is still pending. Could you tell me when it will be paid?
also: Could you check the status of my claim from 3 May?
weak: This is very unprofessional, nobody in HR does any work.
Hi, any update? Pls check.
why: Give the date and ask one clear question. Say 'for a month', not 'since'.

situation: You're opening a short presentation to senior managers.
say: So basically, today I will be discussing about the project.
better: I have one ask today: approval to hire two more testers. Here's why.
also: In short: we're two weeks behind, and here's how we catch up.
weak: Good morning everyone, so basically, actually, what I'm trying to say is...
Okay so, umm, I'll just start. This is the slide.
why: Open with your main point. And it's 'discuss the project', not 'discuss about'.

situation: A client wants everything by Monday, and you can't deliver all of it.
say: Sure, no problem, we will try to manage.
better: We can't do all of it by Monday. We can deliver the login page Monday and the rest by Friday. Does that work?
also: Monday is tight. Which part do you need first?
weak: Okay done, it will be there by Monday, don't worry.
That's impossible, you should have told us earlier.
why: Promise only what you can deliver, and offer a real option.

situation: You notice a mistake in a colleague's sales figures.
say: Your numbers are wrong. Please check before sending.
better: Quick check: I think the March total should be ₹4.2 lakh, not ₹2.4. Could you confirm?
also: I might be wrong, but the March figure looks swapped. Can you take a look?
weak: Very careless. Please be serious about your work.
Sorry to say, but maybe, I'm not sure, something could be off somewhere...
why: Point to the exact error, gently, and let them fix it.

situation: A colleague keeps cutting you off while you're speaking in a meeting.
say: Excuse me, let me complete na!
better: Can I just finish this point? Then I'd like to hear yours.
also: One second, Vikram. Let me finish, then over to you.
weak: Please don't interrupt me, it's very rude.
Oh sorry, you go ahead. (And you never finish.)
why: Hold your turn calmly and promise them theirs.

situation: An interviewer asks why you want to leave your current job.
say: My current company has no growth and the manager is very bad.
better: I've learnt a lot there, but I want to work on bigger products, and this role offers that.
also: I'm looking for more ownership, which I think I'd get here.
weak: Mainly for the salary hike, sir.
Actually there is a lot of politics there, you know how it is.
why: Talk about what you want next, not what you dislike now.

situation: Someone asks you a number in a meeting, and you don't know it.
say: Yes, yes, I think it should be around 20%, roughly.
better: I don't know offhand. I'll check and get back to you by 3 today.
also: Good question. Let me confirm the number and reply on the email thread.
weak: That's not my department, ask someone else.
It should be fine, I'm almost sure.
why: 'I'll check' beats a guess. Give a time and keep it.

situation: A colleague stayed late to fix a bug before your launch.
say: Thanks a lot yaar, you are a life saver.
better: Thanks, Fatima. Your quick fix on the payment bug saved the launch.
also: Big thanks to Fatima for staying late to fix the payment bug.
weak: Thanks to all for everything.
Thanks dear, you are too good.
why: Specific thanks mean more: say what they did and why it mattered.

situation: You want to work from home tomorrow because a plumber is coming.
say: Sir, can I take WFH tomorrow? Some personal work is there.
better: Could I work from home tomorrow? A plumber is coming, and I'll be online all day.
also: I need to be home tomorrow morning. Can I work remotely and join calls as usual?
weak: I'll be WFH tomorrow, some emergency, will be available on phone.
Sir, please sir, just one day only, I'll be online, promise.
why: Ask, give a simple reason, and show you'll still be reachable.
